newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai oil importers must double stocks from Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: Thai oil importers must double stocks from Jan 1.

text.p: Importers of refined oil products into Thailand will be required to double their stockpiles from January 1997 as scheduled, a source from state-run National Energy Policy Office (NEPO) said.
The plan was part of a gradual increase to raise required reserves following the Gulf crisis in 1991, she said on Monday.

In an effort to ensure sufficient reserves for the country, Thailand initially raised the requirement to five percent from three percent of oil supply with a goal of eventually increasing it to 10 percent for imported refined products.
The increase was also aimed at reducing the advantage importers currently had over local producers, the source told Reuters.
At present, local refiners are required to reserve five percent of their crude imports and another five percent of their refined products, for a total of 10 percent of their oil supply.
But importers currently only have to reserve five percent of the refined products they bring into the country.
"There have been some complaints. However, we believe this is a sensible step to make. It's fair and it benefits the country," the NEPO source said.
Thailand imported 181,570 barrels per day (bpd) of refined products in the first seven months of this year, down 7.5 percent from the same period in 1995.
The country's refined product imports declined as two new refineries ramped up operations.
